title: Elephant on the road ahead? 3 rules

scenes.headline: Wild elephant on the road ahead? Do this.
Stay in the vehicle
scenes.body: In protected areas, stopping to get out or feed animals is an offence. The vehicle is your only barrier.

scenes.headline: Never surprise one
scenes.body: Elephants startled by a person close up may panic and charge. Avoid forest-edge paths after dark.

scenes.headline: Give way and stay quiet
scenes.body: Never block its path. No horns, no shouting, no selfies. Wait well back until it has crossed.

caption:
In Karnataka, elephants cross highways along forest corridors.

In Valparai, Tamil Nadu, an SMS and local-TV alert system tells people where elephants are each day, so they can take another route and avoid surprise encounters.

Source: Mongabay; Mongabay-India.  Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Card-led how-to (big step numbers) on a safety skill our trip participants actually need; rules drawn from forest-department enforcement and NCF's conflict work. Photos are generic Asian elephants, no behaviour claimed.
